entities.name: Tyrannion of Amisus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Tyrannion of Amisus was a Greek grammarian brought to Rome as a war captive and slave, known for his significant contributions to the field of grammar and his pupil relationship with Tyrannion the Younger.

  Born into slavery in Amisus, a city in ancient Cilicia, Tyrannion was later sold to a Roman patrician, where he began his studies and developed a reputation as a skilled grammarian. He traveled extensively throughout the Mediterranean, teaching and meeting with prominent scholars of his time.

  Tyrannion's work in grammar and philology had a lasting impact on the development of the field, with his pupil Tyrannion the Younger continuing his work and building upon his discoveries. Tyrannion's legacy can be seen in the many scholars who followed in his footsteps, contributing to the growth and refinement of the subject.

  In the end, Tyrannion's life was marked by his dedication to the pursuit of knowledge and his contributions to the advancement of human understanding, leaving behind a lasting legacy that continues to be felt today.
